summary: Charles Willemen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology, having studied under William Reynolds Beal Acker. He held a professorial post at Ghent University (attested 1999–2001).

Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and Indology. After earning a law doctorate at the University of Liège in 1855, he taught at KU Leuven and Université catholique de Louvain from 1871 to 1899.
Chatral Sangye Dorje worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Sera Khandro, Dorje Dradul, and Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, whom he later succeeded.

Chatsumarn Kabilsingh worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, earning degrees from Visva-Bharati, McMaster, and Magadh Universities. She taught in the Department of Philosophy and Religion at Thammasat University from circa 1973 to 2000.

Chen-kuo Lin is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at Temple University in 1991. He served as Professor and Distinguished Professor at National Chengchi University and held the European Chair of Chinese Studies at Leiden University.
Cheng Huang held posts at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China, UT Southwestern Medical Center, and Southern Methodist University.
Cheng Yen is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who became a disciple of Yinshun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.
Cheryl A. Crowley specializes in Japanology. She studied under Linda H. Chance, William R. LaFleur, Philip Boas Yampolsky, and Ryuichi Abe.
Chhime Rigdzing specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and held a post at Visva-Bharati University.

Chhimed Rigdzin worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying under Choying Khyabdel. He conducted research at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (circa 1954–1957) and served as Professor of Tibetan at Visva-Bharati University (circa 1957–1987).

Chi Chen Ho works in Buddhist studies and sinology. Ho earned a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., studied under Hsuan Hua, and served as a teaching assistant at UCLA.

Chi-chiang Huang specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned a PhD from the University of Arizona in 1986 under doctoral supervisor Jing-shen Tao and also studied under Robert M. Gimello.

Chi-wah Chan works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1993, studying under Robert E. Buswell Jr. and Benjamin A. Elman, and was a teaching assistant at CUHK.

Chia Theng Shen was active in Buddhist studies. He held a post at the Buddhist Association of the United States from circa 1964 to 2007 and founded the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions.
Chie Ikeya specializes in history and archaeology. She earned a PhD from Cornell University in 2006, where she studied under David K. Wyatt.
Chien Y. Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies. Hsu studied under doctoral supervisors Leslie S. Kawamura and James B. Apple, as well as under traditional teacher Zhenhua.

Chien-hsing Ho specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. His academic posts include Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Nanhua University (attested 2014) and a position at Academia Sinica (attested 2018).

Chih-fu Li specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He served as Director of the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2007), later becoming its honorary director upon retiring in December 2006.
Chih-mien Adrian Tseng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned a PhD from McMaster University under James A. Benn and serves on the faculty at Fo Guang University.

Chijo Akamatsu was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Bunzaburo Matsumoto and at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Keijo Imperial, Ryukoku, Koyasan, Hanazono, and Yamaguchi Universities.
